skill-git.title: Git & GitHub for Production Teams
skill-git.summary: Hands-on guide to distributed version control, branching strategies (Gitflow), cherry-picking, pull request etiquette, and conflict resolution.

quiz.question: Which command allows you to integrate changes from 'main' into your feature branch while maintaining a linear commit history?
quiz.explanation: git rebase replays your branch commits on top of the tip of main, keeping history clean and linear.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of a `.gitignore` file?
options: To delete untracked files automatically from disk
To specify intentionally untracked files (build artifacts, secrets, virtualenvs) that Git should ignore
To encrypt sensitive passwords before pushing to GitHub
To prevent teammates from pushing to the main branch
quiz.explanation: .gitignore prevents environment files (.env), node_modules, and binary artifacts from being committed.

quiz.question: If you need to apply a single specific commit from another branch into your current branch, which command do you use?
quiz.explanation: git cherry-pick applies the changes introduced by one or more existing commits to your active HEAD.

skill-rest-apis.title: FastAPI & RESTful API Architecture
skill-rest-apis.summary: Master modern Python web backend development using FastAPI, Pydantic type safety, asynchronous route handlers, CORS, and dependency injection.

quiz.question: Which HTTP status code should a REST API return when a client successfully creates a new resource?
quiz.explanation: HTTP 201 Created signifies that the request succeeded and a new resource has been created.

quiz.question: What role does Pydantic play in FastAPI?
options: Data validation, schema declaration, and automatic JSON serialization/deserialization
CSS layout rendering for web templates
quiz.explanation: Pydantic enforces Python type hints at runtime to validate request payloads and generate OpenAPI documentation.

quiz.question: What is the difference between HTTP PUT and HTTP PATCH?
options: PUT creates a resource, PATCH deletes it
PUT replaces the entire entity representation, whereas PATCH applies partial modifications
PUT is idempotent, PATCH cannot be sent over HTTPS
There is no functional difference in modern REST
quiz.explanation: PUT is an idempotent full update, while PATCH modifies specific fields without replacing the entire entity.

skill-docker.title: Docker for Developers: From Basics to Containerization
skill-docker.summary: Learn to write optimized Dockerfiles, manage images and volumes, orchestrate multi-container apps with docker-compose, and deploy isolated microservices.

quiz.question: Why should `COPY requirements.txt .` and `RUN pip install` appear before `COPY . .` in a Dockerfile?
options: Docker requires Python packages to be installed before files can exist
To leverage Docker's build cache so dependencies aren't re-downloaded every time application code changes
To reduce root user privileges inside the container
It is required by the Linux kernel
quiz.explanation: Docker caches layer by layer. If source code changes, only layers after COPY . . are rebuilt, preserving the heavy pip install cache.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a Docker Image and a Docker Container?
options: An Image is a running instance; a Container is the static binary blueprint
An Image is the immutable snapshot/blueprint; a Container is a live, running instance of an image
Images are for Linux; Containers are for Windows
An Image holds the database; a Container holds the frontend
quiz.explanation: An image is a read-only template with instructions; a container is a runnable instance with an isolated filesystem and process space.

quiz.question: Which command runs a container in detached (background) mode and maps host port 8080 to container port 80?
quiz.explanation: -d runs the container detached, and -p host_port:container_port forwards inbound traffic.

skill-pandas.title: Python for Data Analysis (Pandas & NumPy Deep Dive)
skill-pandas.summary: Master data manipulation: handling missing values, multi-level indexing, GroupBy aggregation, merging datasets, and time-series resampling.

quiz.question: Which method in Pandas computes summary statistics (count, mean, std, min, percentiles, max) for numeric columns?
quiz.explanation: df.describe() generates comprehensive descriptive statistics for all numerical columns in a DataFrame.

quiz.question: What is the most efficient way to perform computations across millions of rows in Pandas?
options: Iterating with a standard Python `for index, row in df.iterrows():` loop
Using vectorized operations or NumPy broadcasting
Converting the DataFrame to a list of dictionaries
quiz.explanation: Vectorized operations execute in compiled C routines (NumPy/BLAS), running 50x to 100x faster than Python row-by-row iteration.

quiz.question: Which function is used to pivot and aggregate long-format data into a multi-dimensional summary table?
quiz.explanation: df.pivot_table() creates a spreadsheet-style pivot table with custom aggregation functions (sum, mean, count).

skill-embedded-c.title: Embedded C Programming & Memory Architecture
skill-embedded-c.summary: Deep dive into volatile pointers, memory-mapped registers, bitwise manipulation, interrupt service routines, and linker scripts.

quiz.question: Why is the `volatile` keyword essential when declaring pointers to hardware peripheral registers?
options: To allocate the pointer inside Flash ROM instead of SRAM
To instruct the compiler NOT to optimize away reads/writes, because the hardware register value can change asynchronously outside program flow
To make the variable thread-safe automatically without mutexes
To enable floating-point math support on 8-bit microcontrollers
quiz.explanation: Without volatile, optimizing compilers will cache register reads into CPU registers, missing real-time hardware status changes.

quiz.question: How do you set bit 4 of an 8-bit register `REG` to 1 without altering any other bits?
quiz.explanation: Bitwise OR with (1 << 4) sets bit 4 to 1 while leaving all other bits untouched.

quiz.question: Why should Interrupt Service Routines (ISRs) be designed to be as short and fast as possible?
options: Because microcontrollers shut down if an ISR takes more than 1 millisecond
To avoid blocking lower-priority interrupts and prevent timing jitter in real-time deadlines
Because ISRs cannot access global variables
To conserve battery charge in sleep mode
quiz.explanation: Long ISRs delay critical system events and degrade real-time responsiveness. Heavy work should be deferred to task queues.
